title: When should you make your game publicly available?
author: liatris4405
selftext:
Recently, I've noticed a growing trend of people using AI to decompile and analyze games in order to create mods and other projects. I've even seen videos on this sub where people analyze two different games and combine elements from both.

This has made me wonder when I should make the game I'm developing available to the public.

For example, the current strategy of releasing a demo early to build up Steam wishlists seems to be increasingly at odds with the risk of having your game decompiled and analyzed.

My own game isn't particularly innovative, so I'm not too worried about it personally. But I feel like this could become an increasingly important issue as AI continues to advance.

I can think of a few options:

1. **Business as usual.** Don't worry about it and follow the traditional approach.
2. **Skip the demo and launch in Early Access.** Make the game available relatively early, but as a paid product.
3. **No demo, no Early Access.** Keep the game itself completely private until the official release date.
4. **Something else?**

What do you all think?

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body:
I think the actual risk of someone stealing your game before it is released is massively overblown to be honest. Assuming you don't release the whole thing, there's no way for the person to know beyond what you've shown what the game will do. And the logistics of people cloning games before they are released don't really make sense. There are thousands of games waiting to be released. Nobody is going to use all of their opus or OAI quota to steal games, badly, at any scale. It just doesn't make economic sense.

I suspect the current "I just stole your game" trend is nothing more than goading for a reaction.

replies.author: Early_Flamingo5337
replies.body: I agree with you. Is a typical early dev thought, but no one will "steal" a game from a indie dev,  people only steal success, not ideas

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body: I mean look at all the meccha chameleon clones out there that nobody cares about. I think the opportunity cost of not promoting your game is way higher.

replies.author: smileyforall220
replies.body: Also if you use Claude or Charcot, your code base is already “in the cloud” aka others can already be using your concepts and ideas based off the new aggregate training data you have it while building

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body:
I'm not sure that really holds up. If you code a game using opus 5.5 or an OAI, that won't mean that those models now remember your game for all users. Anthropic also lets you opt out of your sessions being used for training on newer model. 

Even if you were, your session is basically a blip in the training data, it's not going to remember your game from scratch even if it was included in the training data.

replies.author: smileyforall220
replies.body: What I mean is the methods you used to achieve your goal, aka your potentially unique problem solving ability is what gets remembered. Basically the next version of your game it spits out has a little bit more of your game in it. If I invent a fly fishing drag racing game, a genre that has never existed, now it does and it has a blueprint of how to recreate it for the next person

replies.author: tipsystatistic
replies.body:
Except They’re stealing demos and developing on top of them And superseding the original:

https://www.polygon.com/bills-must-be-paid-steam-demo-chinese-clone-release-controversy/

Stealing games is so easy to do. I imagine this will become a business model where farms use agents to decomp games and see what sticks.

https://voltekplay.itch.io/diapers-please/devlog/915268/one-video-with-full-story-of-our-game-theft

comments.author: Ok-Pirate5732
comments.body:
People who do this are trying to chase a quick buck, and target viral successes. They also target easy to clone games. 

If your game is successful enough where these dudes would want to copy it, and it's sufficiently complex/polished, you probably don't have anything to worry about.

replies.author: tipsystatistic
replies.body:
It’s the early release that’s getting some indie devs. One guy released demo on itch. it was stolen and the they developed on top of it added more levels and features and released it.

It’s now considered the better/official game.

Thieves are browsing Steam and Itch, looking for good ideas/mechanics to steal.

replies.author: ffxivthrowaway03
replies.body:
If that's all it takes to make a "better" version of your game to the point of them stealing the entire thing, then your game is not sufficiently complex/polished.  Someone YOLO ripping your game should not be able to understand your vision and design just from that, and there should be a stark contrast in direction, feel, and quality between the two.

If you're making Candy Crush then yeah, someone can rip that and shit out 1000 AI generated extra "levels".  If you're making something that isn't already just a low-concept clone of an existing viral success then you shouldn't have to worry about this because they'll have *no idea* how to #RestOfTheOwl your game and it'd still be a ton of work even if they did.  These people don't want to work, they want to churn slop for a quick buck.

You'll also want to make sure you have your legal ducks in a row.  If someone is literally stealing your game's name, NPC dialogue, cutscenes, etc it should be trivial for you to prove that those are *your* IP and get them shut down.

replies.author: tipsystatistic
replies.body:
That’s a pretty broad generalization and assumption. 

Not sure the makers of the games that have been ripped off would agree that they’re just “low concept clones”. But you sound like an expert on the topic, so I’m sure you know better than they do.

https://www.polygon.com/bills-must-be-paid-steam-demo-chinese-clone-release-controversy/

replies.author: ffxivthrowaway03
replies.body:
A pretty broad generalization, like "it happened to this one game therefor it's an epidemic issue across the entire industry?"

Mechanics and ideas are easy to steal, you don't need AI to do that and never have.  Exactly like the link you just provided - it's *literally* just a clicker game where you click to smash piggy banks and you're out here acting like someone ripped off the next Grand Theft Auto.  It's *already* just a mild iteration of a million other clicker games.

You don't want some Chinese kid with Deepseek to clone your game, aim your sights higher than "click pigs to make number go up."

comments.author: FreakyChest
comments.body:
You still want to make a demo and such, its great for marketing. Possibly limiting what you show or the demo until your closer to complete like month or so out or a few months.

I feel the one good thing, people that are just stealing work, usually only know how to do low quality junk otherwise they wouldn't have to steal ideas and such. So just make sure to promote your game and get it out there. The more people know of your game and work the harder ot is for someone to take your work. Lots of gamers I feel try to help take down copies or stolen work.

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body:
distribution and awareness is an issue for everyone so market as soon as u can. Ppl now posting here , vibecode , claude code , and other sub reddit to gain traction , multiplied with weekly dev logs.  
  
If your game is indistinguishable from it's clone you likely had slop or a tech demo.

comments.author: thecrustycrap
comments.body: People stealing demos when they find the thread filled with people saying they wishlisted it too

comments.author: mridlen
comments.body: I'm working on what I thought would be a fun weekend project - getting Super Mario World recoded into python (that's only step 1... I want to add features). Finally getting close to feature parity after several weeks. It's not as cheap or effortless as people would have you believe. Then you run into legal problems with using assets. You can't release a game with copyrighted assets in it and expect not to get sued. You would need to generate new assets that are legally distinct.
